subject: Discovery Recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs - Acme Analytics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme-analytics.com>, Tom Baker <tom@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Aisha Rahman <aisha@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs - Acme Analytics

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call so we have shared alignment before the technical deep dive: 

Pain points discussed
- Monthly token costs with current providers (OpenAI/Anthropic) are ballooning as usage grows.
- Vendor lock-in: custom tooling and rate limits make migrations risky.
- Embeddings/semantic search consistency across models; current vector formats tied to vendor glue.
- Latency spikes for chat-support flows during peak hours (affects SLA to customers).

Current stack (as described)
- Primary inference: OpenAI (gpt-4o/gpt-4o-mini for chat) + Anthropic for safety-sensitive flows.
- Embeddings: OpenAI's text-embedding-3-small for search/semantic matching.
- Orchestration: custom routing layer that splits traffic by model/provider, some caching in Redis.
- Security: customer data stored in GCP; using vendor-provided keys and enterprise contracts.

Success criteria for migration
- Reduce per-token inference spend by ~30-50% while preserving acceptable quality for customer-facing chat.
- Maintain or improve latency (target: median <150ms per token in production for chat flows).
- API compatibility for function-calling / streaming and embeddings format so minimal product changes required.
- Ability to run in a VPC/private deployment for regulated customers.

Compatibility requirements we called out
- Function-calling / structured response support or a clear migration path.
- Streaming token output (partial tokens) to keep current UX.
- Embedding format that maps to existing vector store (they use cosine, 1536-d currently).

Model shortlist (initial candidates)
- Llama-3 family (quantized 70B candidate for quality-critical paths)
- Mistral-Instruct / Mixtral variants for cost-sensitive instructions
- OpenAssistant / community-moderated instruction models for fallback / bulk inference

Next steps (proposed)
1) Aisha to run a technical deep dive / benchmark session (incl. streaming + embeddings parity) — propose 60-90 min.
2) Acme to share representative prompt set + sample payloads (anonymized).
3) Redwood to provide initial cost/throughput estimate and a short PoC plan for dedicated or private deployment.
4) Security questionnaire and SOC2 evidence (we requested initial evidence during call).

Attachments: Redwood-solution-one-pager.pdf (one-pager), SOC2-evidence-request.xlsx (requested fields).

Please reply if anything above is incorrect or missing. If this looks good, can you share a sample prompt set and a couple of anonymized payloads so we can scope the benchmark?

Thanks — talk soon.

—
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
https://redwood.com
From: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme-analytics.com>

Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs - Acme Analytics

Marissa — thanks for the thorough recap, this captures things well. A few additional data points from our side to help scope:

- Current usage: ~120M tokens/month total (chat + generation), ~30% of tokens are embedding requests for search/recall.
- Peak concurrency: roughly 120 concurrent chat sessions during US morning peak.
- Latency target: <150ms median is correct; 95th percentile ideally under 600ms.
- Primary use cases: customer support chat (high quality) and semantic search for internal tooling (cost sensitive).
- Security: we must keep data in our GCP project for now; VPC peering or private deployment is preferred.

We can share a sanitized prompt set and 10-15 representative payloads by EOD Wednesday (2026-03-04). Also happy to schedule the technical deep dive —Wed/Thu afternoons PST work best for our infra and ML Eng folks.

One note on embeddings: our vector store expects 1536-d vectors (cosine). If Redwood's embeddings path differs, we need a deterministic migration plan.

Looking forward to the benchmark plan and cost estimate.

Cheers,
Alice Nguyen
Head of ML Platforms, Acme Analytics
alice@acme-analytics.com
